title: We put a persistent AI character in a browser racing game instead of another chat window
author: ChemicalPresent8796
selftext:
I'm one of the devs at Virtual Dawn in Finland. We've spent a lot of time building AI characters with memory, relationships and world state that persist outside the LLM context. But after a while we got bored of demonstrating it with yet another chat box.

So this is Neon Drift. You race an AI companion/rival in a playable browser world. Draft behind her car to build the Sync Meter, trigger a boost and try to pass. The wider Virtual Twilight project uses that same character/state layer across conversations and different game worlds.

Actual short gameplay, not a cinematic:
https://www.youtube.com/shorts/BY4fsZUNJtw

Try the browser game (desktop mode available, or Quest in headset browser):
https://www.virtualtwilight.app/games/neon-drift?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=community&utm_campaign=neon_drift_aigamedev_sep19

The wider Virtual Twilight platform is for adults 18+. There's a free tier; it's an ongoing indie build, not a finished giant game library.

The technical challenge we keep coming back to: game state needs to stay authoritative even when the LLM is improvising dialogue. It's much harder when the same character needs to remain coherent outside the conversation.
